title: Representability, flat restriction, properness and boundary of a space blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $T$ be an algebraic space and let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal. The blowup $p:T^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T\to T$ is representable and proper. For any flat morphism $h:A\to T$, the base change $A\times_TT^{\prime}\to A$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is canonically the blowup of $A$ in $\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_A)$. In particular this holds for open immersions; if $A$ is a scheme this is the ordinary scheme blowup, with the finite-type Zariski ideal corresponding to that etale ideal [pqf-def-coherent, lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. If $U=T\setminus V(\mathcal K)$, the restriction $p^{-1}U\to U$ is an isomorphism. The ideal $\operatorname{im}(p^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_{T^{\prime}})$ is locally generated by a non-zero-divisor, and its zero subspace is $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$; thus this is an effective Cartier divisor. Moreover $p^{-1}U$ is schematically dense in $T^{\prime}$: for its open inclusion $j$, the sheaf map $\mathcal O_{T^{\prime}}\to j_*\mathcal O_{p^{-1}U}$ on the small etale site is injective. On an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ with ideal $K\subseteq R$, the pullback is $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{d\geq0}K^d)$, covered by the affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}R[K/a]$ for $a\in K$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. Empty centres and the zero ideal are allowed.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$ with $\mathcal K^0=\mathcal O_T$, products induced by multiplication of ideals. The affine-chart calculus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] computes tensor products and images, so induction on $d$, with $\mathcal K^d$ the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal K^{d-1}\otimes\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_T$, makes each power quasi-coherent and identifies its restriction on $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$ with $K^d$. Here a tensor product of quasi-coherent modules is quasi-coherent because tensoring two local presentations $\mathcal O^{(I)}\to\mathcal O^{(J)}\to M\to0$ gives one, by right exactness of the tensor product and its commutation with coproducts. Arbitrary direct sums remain quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests] to this graded algebra. Its scheme-test conclusion proves that $T'=P_T(\mathcal R)$ is an algebraic space representable over $T$. For an affine etale $g:V\to T$ the comparison is $V\times_TT'\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_V((g^*\mathcal R)_{\mathrm{Zar}})\simeq\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_dK^d)$: the etale tensor pullback $g^*\mathcal R$ is the restriction $\mathcal R|_V$ by [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], the Zariski module is its restriction to Zariski opens by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], its sections on $V$ are $\bigoplus_dK^d$ by the filtered-colimit clause of the chart calculus, and the relative Proj over the affine $V$ is $\operatorname{Proj}$ of these sections by [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. Finite type of $K$ on every such chart follows from the finite-type criterion in the affine-chart calculus, without a Noetherian assumption.

For flat $h:A\to T$, put $\mathcal J=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_A)$. Construct the degree-$d$ map $\beta_d:h^*\mathcal K^d\to\mathcal J^d$ by multiplication, locally $b\otimes x\mapsto b\,h^\sharp(x)$. Refine an etale atlas of $A$ by scheme charts $W\to A$ mapping to etale affine charts $V\to T$; the refinements exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Each $W\to V$ is flat by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. The chart tensor formula and composition comparison of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization], and the scheme pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], identify $\beta_d$ on these charts with the degree-$d$ map of [def-nagata-flat-pullback-rees-map]. That map is an isomorphism in every degree by [lemma-nagata-flat-pullback-rees]. The formula commutes with restrictions and sends a product of tensors to the tensor of the product, so the maps give a unital graded algebra map $\beta:h^*\mathcal R\to\bigoplus_d\mathcal J^d$. It is an isomorphism: its local inverses agree wherever both are defined because each is inverse to the same map, and the sheaf axiom glues them. Quasi-coherence of pullbacks is [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], and that of images and powers is the chart calculus from step 1.

The arbitrary-base-change comparison and graded-isomorphism clause of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests], applied to $\beta$, give
$$A\times_TT'\simeq P_A(h^*\mathcal R)\simeq P_A(\bigoplus_d\mathcal J^d)=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}A.$$
These are over $A$ and canonical, since the comparisons on scheme tests are the relative-Proj comparisons and $\beta_d$ has the specified tensor formula. For an open subspace the same conclusion follows directly by restriction: the structure ring, ideals and their powers restrict, so the pulled-back graded algebra is the Rees algebra of the restricted ideal. If $A$ is a scheme, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies the etale ideal with a Zariski quasi-coherent ideal, and [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] makes it finite type in the Zariski topology. The images of any finite local generating family generate $\mathcal J$, so this ideal is finite type. The scheme-test formula identifies its relative Proj with the ordinary scheme blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model]: over each affine open $V\subseteq A$ the relative Proj restricts to $\operatorname{Proj}$ of its sections [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] and the local model is the affine blowup $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_{A_V}(J_V))$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup], so both are the same Rees Proj, and the comparisons agree on further restrictions and hence glue. This also verifies that the construction of step 1 is exactly the etale descent of the ordinary blowups stipulated in the statement.

Choose an affine etale covering $\{V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to T\}$. Step 1 identifies the pullback of $p$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_dK_i^d)$, which is the affine blowup [def-nagata-affine-blowup] in the finitely generated ideal $K_i$; this is proper by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-proper], using the agreement of scheme and space properness in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. To justify properness descent without assuming a scheme target, fix any scheme $W\to T$. Its pulled-back covering $W_i=W\times_TV_i\to W$ is a jointly surjective family of etale schemes by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; it is fppf by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The pullback of $p_W$ over $W_i$ is a base change of the proper map over $V_i$, hence proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. The scheme-target covering criterion [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] therefore makes $p_W$ proper. Since this holds for every scheme $W\to T$, [lem-sfb-space-proper-arbitrary-scheme-tests] makes $p$ proper. No quasi-compactness of $T$ or of the whole etale atlas was used.

proof.text: On $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, choose finitely many generators $K=(a_0,\ldots,a_r)$, allowing the single generator $0$ when $K=0$. The finite affine covering [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] identifies the blowup with a union of the standard charts $C_i=R[K/a_i]$. For any $a\in K$, the chart isomorphism [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart] with its specified map [def-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-map] gives $\operatorname{Spec}R[K/a]\simeq D_+(at)$ over $V$. Thus all $a\in K$ also give an affine covering, and these are the asserted charts of $T'$ over $V$. The base-changed etale covering of $T$ covers $T'$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and open inclusions are etale since they are locally identity maps, so these are jointly surjective etale scheme charts of $T'$.

Let $U=T\setminus V(\mathcal K)$. On each affine etale chart $V$ of $T$, the map $p^{-1}U\to U$ becomes the restriction of the ordinary affine blowup away from $V(K)$, which is an isomorphism by [lemma-nagata-affine-blowup-complement]. The inverse maps on these covering sheaves agree on overlaps: the composites with $p$ are the identity, so uniqueness of inverses forces equality. Morphisms between sheaves glue along an etale cover by the sheaf condition, and the glued inverse has both composites the identity after the same cover, hence globally. This proves $p^{-1}U\simeq U$ without imposing density of $U$ in $T$.

By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], the ideal of $T'\times_TV(\mathcal K)$ is precisely $\mathcal L=\operatorname{im}(p^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_{T'})$. On the chart $C=R[K/a]$, [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal] says $KC=(a)$ and [lemma-nagata-chart-generator-regular] says multiplication by $a$ on $C$ is injective. Thus $\mathcal L$ is locally generated on the small etale site by a non-zero-divisor, exactly the effective Cartier condition in the statement. Its zero subspace is $p^{-1}V(\mathcal K)$ by the cited ideal correspondence, and its complementary open on this chart is $D(a)$. This argument uses no domain, reducedness or non-zero-divisor assumption on $a$ in $R$.

It remains to check injectivity of $\mathcal O_{T'}\to j_*\mathcal O_{p^{-1}U}$ on the entire small etale site. On a chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ from step 5 the open is $D(a)$ and $a$ acts injectively on $C$. For any affine etale scheme $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat] makes $B$ flat over $C$, and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection], applied to multiplication by $a$ on $C$, makes multiplication by $a$ injective on $B$. If $s\in B$ vanishes on $D(a)$, its image in $B_a$ is zero; the defining localization relation gives $a^ns=0$ for some $n$, hence $s=0$. For an arbitrary etale object $W\to T'$, pull back the covering of step 5 and refine by affine opens. These refinements are etale over the chart schemes by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. The preceding argument annihilates every restriction of a section in the kernel. The separatedness axiom for the structure sheaf then annihilates the original section. This proves the required sheaf monomorphism, including when $T'$ is empty.
